verdicts.reviewer_notes: Fifth review, done from scratch. I fetched the signed PDF (gov.ca.gov FINAL-N-9-26-AI-EO-9.18.26-SIGNED.pdf) and read all 3 pages of its text. VERIFIED against the order: it is EO N-9-26, signed and sealed 'this 18th day of September 2026', and issued 'to become effective immediately' (so event_date 2026-09-18 and stage in_force are correct). Para 1: no later than May 1, 2027, the Government Operations Agency shall complete the requirements of Gov. Code 8898.1 and develop application requirements, procedures and criteria for independent verification organizations and publicly post them, 'as required by law' (matches). Para 2: no later than December 1, 2027, the Agency shall complete 11549.82(a) and begin taking the actions required by 11549.82(b) (matches). Para 3: the Government Operations Agency, 'in consultation with the Governor's Office of Emergency Services', shall by November 16, 2026 'submit to my office recommendations, developed in consultation with national experts, addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state laws regarding AI safety and security, including at least' (a) large frontier developers embedding designated IVOs onsite for periodic audits and evaluations, (b) independent verification of the safety frameworks, transparency reports and risk assessments that frontier AI companies must file, (c) a 'kill switch' for frontier models whose efficacy an IVO verifies on an ongoing basis, and (d) updating the definition of critical safety incidents to include a range of loss-of-control incidents. The summary's sub-items (a) to (d) match. The no-enforceable-rights clause matches. The 23 Sept 2026 gov.ca.gov release (re-fetched) is consistent: the order directs GovOps to 'accelerate the implementation timelines for SB 813 and AB 1405' and to convene experts. Both sources are from the Governor's office, so primary tier is correct. High confidence fits because the primary text was read in full. Not a duplicate: the only related file is content/items/2026-09/us-ca-sb-813-ab-1405-ai-third-party-verification.json, which covers the separate 9 Sept bill signing. Topics fit. Type 'regulation' is consistent with how this run types the other executive order, since ITEM_TYPES has no executive-order value. PROBLEMS: (1) Who submits: the summary says it 'directs the agency, with the Governor's Office of Emergency Services, to submit recommendations'. That reads as a joint submission. Under the order, GovOps alone submits, in consultation with Cal OES. This also disagrees with the instrument entry, which phrases it correctly. (2) What is recommended: the summary says 'recommendations ... on amendments to state AI safety law'. The order asks for recommendations 'addressing the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments to existing state laws regarding AI safety and security', developed in consultation with national experts. The item drops the feasibility/efficacy framing, so it reads as if the order asks for amendments to be recommended. (3) Title: 'directs work on independent verification, a frontier-model kill switch and loss-of-control incident reporting' overstates the order for the kill switch and loss-of-control items. For those, the order directs only feasibility and efficacy recommendations. The press release's 'advance the creation of a kill switch' wording is the governor's own characterisation, not the order's text. (4) why_it_matters says 'possible amendments to California's frontier AI law' (singular). The order says 'existing state laws regarding AI safety and security' (plural) and does not name SB 53 in its operative paragraphs. 'Sets the timetable for the state's independent verification regime' is acceptable only loosely: the order sets 'no later than' deadlines for GovOps, and the order itself does not say what 11549.82 covers. Tightening this is recommended but not required.

verdicts.reviewer_notes: Checked each sentence against the full text of the signed order PDF (3 pages, read directly). Summary: the date (18 September 2026, from the signature block) is correct. The Para 1 wording (complete Gov. Code 8898.1; develop and publicly post IVO application requirements, procedures and criteria, 'as required by law'; by 1 May 2027) is correct. Para 2 (complete 11549.82(a), begin 11549.82(b) actions, by 1 December 2027) is correct. Para 3 is correct on who submits what to whom: GovOps, 'in consultation with' Cal OES, submits to the Governor's office by 16 November 2026 recommendations on 'the technical feasibility and potential efficacy of amendments' to state AI safety and security law. The no-enforceable-rights statement is correct. key_obligations: all three match paras 1 to 3. The four listed recommendation topics match sub-items (a) to (d). Two acceptable simplifications: the kill-switch item omits 'on an ongoing basis', and the summary omits that the recommendations are 'developed in consultation with national experts'. Neither changes the meaning. kind 'executive_order' fits the protocol definition (an order by a head of government). status 'in_force' and the single 2026-09-18 timeline entry ('signed and effective immediately') match 'to become effective immediately' and the signature date. The timeline source_url is the signed order (primary). The name's parenthetical describes the order fairly and neutrally. No duplicate: content/instruments/ has only us-ca-sb-53 and us-ca-sb-1119 for California, and a grep for N-9-26, 'kill switch' and 'independent verification organi' finds nothing in content/instruments/. Consistency with the item: the instrument states the OES role and the feasibility/efficacy framing correctly. The item currently does not; see the item's required changes.
